In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the most appropriate analytical methodology for solving a given problem should be chosen on the basis of its performance, as assessed by means of appropriate figures of merit, and not on the basis of the mathematical model that is used for the data processing.

, for the sake of clarity and reproducibility of analytical data, it is strongly recommended that the authors of scientific papers on analytical calibration report all the relevant analytical figures of merit, including the analytical figures of merit of the calibration models, and that they also provide a detailed description of the calibration procedure and the mathematical model used.

the analytical chemist should always report the analytical calibration data and the analytical figures of merit, and that these should be presented in a way that is clear and easy to understand for the reader.

the present paper should be of interest for analytical chemists and chemical metrologists who wish to improve their analytical procedures and/or their analytical reports.
the analytical chemist should always strive to report the most complete information possible for the results obtained in the analytical process.

, in order to obtain a correct and reliable calibration model, the analyst should carefully consider the following aspects: (1) a proper selection of the analytical methodology; (2) the optimization of the analytical procedure, which is essential for obtaining accurate and precise data; (3) the correct application of calibration techniques and algorithms; and (4) the correct interpretation of calibration results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
analytical calibration is a complex process, which requires a thorough understanding of the experimental conditions and of the analytical figures of merit.
analytical calibration is not a simple matter and that the correct reporting of analytical figures of merits is a crucial issue.
